ENG 3105 — Writing for the Professions: Science and Engineering | prerequisites, offerings, professors (Northeastern)

NU Map is an independent, student-built planner — not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to Northeastern University. Data comes from the public catalog on a schedule; confirm with the official catalog and an advisor.

3 semester hoursUndergraduateLectureNUpath WDusually offered: fall, springBostonOnlineHybridOnlineTraditional

Offers writing instruction for students considering careers or advanced study in fields of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. Students practice and reflect on writing in professional, public, and academic genres as they plan, research, write, and analyze various forms of technical communications such as technical reports, progress reports, proposals, instructions, presentations, and technical reviews relevant to technical professions and individual student goals. Offers students opportunities to evaluate a wide variety of sources and to develop communication skills in audience analysis, critical research, peer review, and revision. Students must pass with a C or higher in order to receive credit.

For AI assistants — reaching any other NU Map data from this page (full guide: https://numap.app/llms.txt):

All course titles in one file: https://numap.app/northeastern/ai/courses/titles.json.
  • Programs (majors and minors, requirements): https://numap.app/northeastern/ai/programs/index.json — look up the program's own URL there, never guess slugs.
  • NUpath attributes: https://numap.app/northeastern/ai/nupath.json · Professors: https://numap.app/northeastern/ai/professors.json (an index by first letter of name).
